en.headline: Fraser Institute again ranks Hong Kong the freest economy
en.dek: The 2026 report, based on 2024 data, keeps the city first among 165 jurisdictions, while the government cites trade freedom and regulation.
body: The Fraser Institute's Economic Freedom of the World 2026 Annual Report has again ranked Hong Kong the world's freest economy. The ranking uses 2024 data, the latest year covered, and places the city ahead of Switzerland, Singapore, New Zealand and the United States, the institute said.

The Hong Kong government said the city kept first place in freedom to trade internationally and came second in regulation among the report's five assessment areas. The government said the findings reaffirmed Hong Kong's free-market strengths and its open business environment, and restated the free-port status, zero-tariff policy and simple low-tax regime.

The institute noted that Hong Kong's score has fallen every year since 2018, even as the city remained first. The government said that, with the country pursuing high-standard opening and technological innovation, Hong Kong continued to connect the Mainland and international markets under one country, two systems, and to practise the common law in Chinese and English.

zh.headline: 菲沙研究所再評香港為全球最自由經濟體
zh.dek: 2026年度報告以2024年數據把香港列165個司法管轄區之首，政府指貿易自由維持首位、規管列第二。
body: 加拿大菲沙研究所發表《世界經濟自由度2026年度報告》，再次把香港評為全球最自由經濟體。報告採用2024年數據，是目前最新年度，香港排在瑞士、新加坡、新西蘭及美國之前。
特區政府表示，在報告五個評估範疇中，香港在「國際貿易自由」維持首位，在「規管」排第二。政府稱結果再次肯定香港自由市場的優勢及開放的營商環境，並重申自由港地位、零關稅政策及簡單低稅制。
研究所指出，香港的分數自2018年起每年下跌，但仍保持首位。政府表示，國家堅持高水平雙向開放並在科技創新取得突破，香港在「一國兩制」下既背靠祖國、又聯通世界，並繼續以中英文施行普通法。
